style_when: the article explains how a system, process or stack actually works — money flows, supply chains, pipelines, an agent assembly line
prompt: Clean isometric cutaway of an H100 accelerator board on a brushed-steel workbench in a server room. Split-screen diptych: left half shows batch-1 decode with a single chunky 4-bit weight module and one thin token path feeding a single matrix-multiply engine; right half shows batch-32 with eight parallel FP8 arithmetic modules and dozens of token streams converging, HBM stacks visible. Axonometric projection, flat muted graphite and steel-blue palette with one safety-yellow accent, thin consistent line weight, one directional light from upper left, generous empty margin, no text, no lettering.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, illegible labels
rationale: The story explains how a system actually works — memory-bound versus compute-bound regimes of GPU quantization — so a technical isometric cutaway can show the internal weight and arithmetic modules rebalancing across batch sizes. It avoids a generic datacenter shot while grounding the abstract speedup tradeoff in recognizable H100 hardware.

core_thesis: A quantization recipe's speedup is the share of your step time that is memory-bound, so 4-bit weights beat 16-bit at batch 1 but 8-bit arithmetic overtakes them at batch 32.
core_conflict: memory-bound single-token decode vs compute-bound multi-sequence throughput; capacity vs speed

review.depicts: A split-screen isometric cutaway showing two accelerator boards on a data-center floor with server racks behind them: the left board has one yellow module with a single thin trace running off it, and the right board has a row of eight blue compute blocks with a bundle of eight parallel traces fanning out through the bracket.
review.reason: The diptych literally stages the article's mechanism — one serial path at batch 1 versus eight parallel paths at batch 32 on GPU boards — so a reader would recognize the batch-scaling comparison, though the 4-bit/8-bit labels and the FP8 crossover are not shown.
